squawks.headline: Japan's 40-year JGB yield falls 6bp to 4.05%
squawks.detail: Japan's 40-year government bond yield is reported 6bp lower at 4.05% in Tokyo trading on 20 October.

squawks.headline: UK Treasury expected to study options for closer long-term ties with the EU, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the Treasury is expected to carry out a study of Britain moving closer to the EU, with Andy Burnham preparing to set out options for the UK's longer-term relationship with the bloc.

squawks.headline: China sells 10-year government bonds at a 1.6057% yield
squawks.detail: Traders say China's finance ministry auctioned 10-year bonds at a yield of 1.6057%, and offered 2-month bills at 1.0316%.

squawks.headline: Bank of England and Bank of Korea widen their partnership on tokenisation
squawks.detail: Yonhap reports that South Korea's central bank and the Bank of England have broadened their cooperation on tokenisation.

squawks.headline: PBOC to offer up to 1 trillion yuan a day in overnight reverse repos from 21 October to 2 November
squawks.detail: China's central bank announced the overnight reverse repo operations for the period. It carried out no 7-day reverse repos on Tuesday.

squawks.headline: Japan's finance minister Katayama says no decision has been made on how to fund the expected rise in defence spending
squawks.detail: Katayama said the government is still discussing defence spending and will look at ways to secure stable funding while keeping a focus on fiscal sustainability.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US and Mexico are very close to a trade deal
squawks.detail: US President Trump said on Monday that Mexico and the United States are very close to agreeing a trade deal, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: China keeps its one-year and five-year loan prime rates at 3.00% and 3.50%, as expected
squawks.detail: The People's Bank of China left its benchmark lending rates unchanged in October, in line with forecasts. Reuters reports that rates have now been held for 17 months in a row.

squawks.headline: Japan's economy minister Kiuchi says he hopes to attend this month's BoJ policy meeting if his schedule allows
squawks.detail: Kiuchi said the government respects the Bank of Japan's autonomy over monetary policy as set out in the BoJ law. He also said he has never considered asking for a vote at a BoJ meeting to be postponed.

squawks.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield holds at 5.14% after a 7bp rise; French unrest weighs on European bonds and the euro
squawks.detail: A market wrap reports the US 10-year yield steady at 5.14% after rising seven basis points, with oil near elevated levels on Middle East supply risks. French political unrest was reported as adding pressure to European bonds and the euro.

squawks.headline: Trump says NATO allies refused to help the US in the Iran war and the US could be forced to leave Europe
squawks.detail: The FT reports that the US President said NATO allies declined to assist in the war with Iran. He also said the US could be forced to leave Europe and called the situation very serious.

squawks.headline: 10-year JGB futures fall 0.22 point in early Tokyo trade ahead of a 20-year bond sale
squawks.detail: Benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond futures fell 0.22 point in early trade. Japan is due to sell 20-year government bonds.

squawks.headline: Trump administration has not approved sending interceptor missiles to Ukraine, Washington Post reports
squawks.detail: According to the Washington Post, the US administration has not approved the transfer of interceptor missiles to Ukraine. Separately, US Vice President Vance said Ukraine should not join NATO.

squawks.headline: UK finance minister Healey rules out raising capital gains tax in the 28 October Budget, the Times reports
squawks.detail: The Times reported on Monday, as cited by Reuters, that John Healey has turned down calls to increase capital gains tax in his first Budget on 28 October. According to the report, he is instead putting economic growth and business investment first.

squawks.headline: Iran's Hormuz management body adds 122 ships to its list of non-compliant vessels
squawks.detail: Iran's Strait of Hormuz Management Organization said it has added 122 ships to its non-compliance list, as Tehran continues to restrict traffic through the strait.

squawks.headline: US Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude stocks fall to 282.7m barrels, the lowest since 1982
squawks.detail: Crude oil held in the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell to 282.7 million barrels last week, the lowest level since 1982.

squawks.headline: US lawmakers oppose Trump's proposed Russian diesel deal; European diesel futures have more than doubled this year
squawks.detail: Trump's proposed deal on Russian diesel is meeting opposition from US lawmakers, and analysts question whether extra supply would bring fuel prices down. Brent is up more than 75% this year and European diesel futures have more than doubled.

squawks.headline: Brent settles at $109.55 a barrel, close to a five-month high, as Middle East tensions weigh on supply
squawks.detail: Brent settled at $109.55 a barrel and moved around a five-month high on supply risks from the Middle East. Gains were reported as limited by a recovery in Hormuz flows and by technical indicators showing the market as overbought.

squawks.headline: Ukrainian officials suspect the US is intermittently limiting intelligence sharing; US Secretary of State Rubio denies any pause
squawks.detail: Ukrainian officials say they suspect the US is restricting intelligence sharing on and off, leaving Ukraine without early warning of Russian missile attacks. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio denies there has been any pause in support.

squawks.headline: Iran summons the EU and German ambassadors, reports say
squawks.detail: Reports say Tehran has summoned the ambassadors of the EU and Germany. Earlier, Iran's foreign minister accused European countries of complicity in the US war with Iran.

squawks.headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says no Russian diesel has been released so far
squawks.detail: US Energy Secretary Wright said Russian diesel has not yet been released. He made the remark during continuing US talks with Russia on diesel.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine could halt strikes on Russian refineries if the US helps supply Patriot missiles
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said Kyiv could stop hitting Russian refineries for a period in exchange for US help with Patriot missiles. He also said the Pentagon is delaying missile deliveries under the PURL programme, and called the US decisions hard to explain.

squawks.headline: Trump says he would discuss Ukraine with China's Xi and calls Xi's stance on the war very fair
squawks.detail: US President Trump said he would be willing to talk to Chinese President Xi about Ukraine and described Xi's position on Ukraine as very fair. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Trump says Russia could have done much more to help Iran
squawks.detail: President Trump made the remark in comments to reporters on Monday evening, alongside further remarks on Ukraine and the protests in France. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Trump says it may be time for someone other than Zelenskiy to negotiate on Ukraine's behalf
squawks.detail: US President Trump said Zelenskiy does not know what he is talking about, and that the US shares intelligence with Ukraine and gives it a lot but gets nothing back. In the same remarks he said Russia had done very little to help Iran and called that positive.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US is negotiating with Russia on Iran and diesel and is open to a trilateral meeting with Russia and China
squawks.detail: Speaking live, the US President said he would schedule a joint meeting with Xi and Putin on the basis of denuclearisation, said Russia has been fine on Ukraine, and said he did not think Zelenskiy wants to end the war. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

squawks.headline: Trump says the Iran situation is good, Putin is staying out of Iran and the US is negotiating with Putin on Ukraine
squawks.detail: In remarks on Monday evening, US President Trump said the situation regarding Iran was good and that Putin was leaving Iran alone. He also said Washington was negotiating with Putin on Ukraine and did not want to break off those talks.

squawks.headline: Iran says its offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within days still stands if the US accepts its conditions
squawks.detail: Iran said the offer to reopen the strait remains available on condition that Washington accepts Tehran's terms. Tensions and attacks around the waterway are continuing.

squawks.headline: IRGC spokesman points to seven major undersea data cables under the Strait of Hormuz in a warning to Iran's enemies
squawks.detail: Iran's Revolutionary Guards spokesman said seven major cables carrying global internet and business data run beneath the Strait of Hormuz, and told the enemy to bear this in mind, Fars News reported. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Israel's finance minister Smotrich calls for annexing Lebanese territory up to current Israeli lines, and further if Hezbollah attacks
squawks.detail: Israeli Finance Minister Smotrich said Israel should annex Lebanon at least up to where its forces are now positioned, and advance as far as Beirut and beyond if Hezbollah attacks again. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: IRGC spokesman says Iran could widen its blockade beyond Hormuz to the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and the Suez Canal
squawks.detail: The Tehran Times reports an IRGC spokesman as saying Iran has not yet fully closed the Strait of Hormuz and could extend the blockade to the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and the Suez Canal. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: WTI crude settles 2.22% higher at $103.66 a barrel, up $2.25
squawks.detail: NYMEX November WTI futures settled at $103.66 a barrel, up $2.25 or 2.22% on the day. November diesel futures settled at $4.9201 a gallon and November gasoline at $3.1914 a gallon.

squawks.headline: US official denies Iran's claim that US forces struck an Iranian naval base
squawks.detail: A US official told a CNN reporter that Iran's claim that the US had struck one of its naval bases is inaccurate. Iran's navy had earlier said US forces hit its Konark base.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz says Berlin is committing more than €500bn by the end of the decade to defence and military infrastructure
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Merz described the programme as the biggest modernisation drive in Germany's recent history. In the same remarks he said Russia and its allies, from North Korea to Iran, are attacking post-war democratic values as well as Ukraine.

squawks.headline: Bank of Japan sees inflation close to its 2% target and is preparing a policy pivot, Nikkei reports
squawks.detail: Nikkei reports that the Bank of Japan judges inflation to be near its 2% target and is getting ready for a change in policy direction.

squawks.headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian says Tehran is ready to settle issues with regional countries through dialogue
squawks.detail: Reports say Pezeshkian stated that Iran has no fundamental differences with countries in the region. Separately, Iran told Russia it welcomes any regional peace initiative.

squawks.headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says the US is converting sanctioned dark tankers into legitimate vessels
squawks.detail: US Energy Secretary Wright said sanctioned tankers are being converted into legitimate tankers. He added that the number converted could run from dozens to hundreds.

squawks.headline: Barclays says its £15bn private credit book meets accounting and capital rules after report of Bank of England scrutiny
squawks.detail: Barclays said its £15 billion private credit exposure was treated in line with accounting and regulatory capital requirements, Reuters reports. The statement follows a report that the Bank of England was examining whether the bank's traders had understated the risk.

squawks.headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says talks with the UK on releasing diesel stocks are continuing
squawks.detail: US Energy Secretary Wright said on Monday that discussions with the UK on diesel stock releases are still under way. No figures or timing were given.

squawks.headline: Lyon imposes a city-centre curfew from 9pm Monday to 6am Tuesday as French unrest continues
squawks.detail: The local prefecture announced the overnight curfew in Lyon city centre. It follows curfews already ordered in Paris, Lille and other northern cities after the riots.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz says there is no rush to decide on ECB posts, though a quick decision could be reached if needed
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said there is no need for a fast decision on ECB positions, but added that agreement on the jobs could be reached quickly if required.

squawks.headline: Brent turns higher on the day and WTI extends gains after Houthis claim attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure
squawks.detail: Brent was last up 0.15% and WTI up 1.5% after the Houthis said they had attacked Saudi infrastructure. Brent had earlier been down 2.43% on the day, below $105 a barrel.

squawks.headline: French authorities extend curfews to Paris, covering Place de la République and Les Halles from 2000 GMT
squawks.detail: BFM TV reports that French authorities have ordered a curfew for the Place de la République and Les Halles areas of Paris from 2000 GMT. It follows earlier curfews in Lille and other northern cities after riots.

squawks.headline: Netanyahu reportedly tells Trump that Israel still has work to finish
squawks.detail: Israel Hayom reports that Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu told US President Trump that Israel's work is not yet complete. The report comes as US-Iran tensions continue.

squawks.headline: Scotiabank expects the Bank of Canada to raise rates by 25bp next week
squawks.detail: Scotiabank expects a 25bp Bank of Canada hike at next week's decision, a report said.

squawks.headline: Adviser to Iran's supreme leader rejects claims that the Strait of Hormuz is open
squawks.detail: An adviser to Iran's supreme leader said claims that the Strait of Hormuz is open have no basis, Tasnim News reported.

squawks.headline: Netanyahu says Trump sees the final removal of the Iranian threat as the key issue
squawks.detail: Israeli PM Netanyahu referred to Trump's support ahead of Israel's elections and said the final removal of the Iranian threat to Israel is the central question, Israel's Channel 14 News reported.

squawks.headline: Houthis claim strikes on Saudi Arabia's Shaybah oilfield and on airports in Riyadh and Abha
squawks.detail: Yemen's Houthi forces say they attacked the Shaybah oilfield, King Khalid airport in Riyadh and Abha airport. The posts do not report any damage to oil output or any market reaction.

squawks.headline: Houthis say they have attacked Saudi energy, airport and military targets, including an Aramco site in Yanbu
squawks.detail: Yemen's Houthi-run forces announced several military operations deep inside Saudi territory, saying the targets included energy facilities, airports and military sites, among them an Aramco site in Yanbu. The batch reports no market reaction.

squawks.headline: IRGC spokesman says new weapons and targets will be revealed in a new phase of the war with the US
squawks.detail: Fars News reported that a spokesman for Iran's Revolutionary Guards said new weapons and targets would be unveiled and that Iran would drive what is left of US power out of the region.

squawks.headline: France to impose 8pm curfew in Lille and other northern cities after riots, reports say
squawks.detail: Reports say France will bring in an 8pm curfew in Lille and other cities in the north of the country. The government had already ordered partial curfews after the riots.

squawks.headline: Iran's first vice president says Tehran has no choice but to take control of the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: Iran's first vice president Aref, cited by state news agency IRNA, said Iran must assert control over Hormuz, and that passage through the strait can be made easier for friendly nations. The posts report no market reaction.

squawks.headline: Iran's navy says US forces have struck its Konark base
squawks.detail: Iran's navy said US forces had carried out a strike on its Konark base. No market reaction was reported alongside the claim.

squawks.headline: Bank of Canada Q3 business survey indicator improves to -0.33; consumers' five-year inflation expectations rise to 3.91%
squawks.detail: The Bank of Canada's Q3 Business Outlook Survey, mostly conducted before Canada-US trade talks collapsed, shows its indicator at -0.33, up from a revised -0.39 in Q2. The share of firms expecting a recession next year fell to 6% from 17%, and 41% expect inflation above 3% over the next two years, down from 44%. In the separate consumer survey, five-year inflation expectations rose to 3.91% from 3.39%, and 53.0% of Canadians expect a recession, down from 54.6%.

squawks.headline: Bank of Canada business survey shows a weaker outlook and higher inflation expectations after Canada-US trade talks failed
squawks.detail: The Bank of Canada's September survey of business leaders shows firms' outlook got worse. Their inflation expectations rose after Canada-US trade talks broke down.

squawks.headline: Yemen's Houthi-run forces threaten Riyadh and say Saudi oil facilities are targets for their missiles
squawks.detail: A military source with the Houthi-run Yemeni armed forces said the Saudi capital would not be safe and that Saudi oil facilities are within missile range, Iran's Fars news agency reported. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: French 10-year yields on course for their biggest one-day rise since March 2025
squawks.detail: A market newswire headline reports the move as French bond selling continues amid political unrest and rioting. No new yield level was given.

squawks.headline: French 10-year yield climbs further to 4.94%, up 16bp on the day
squawks.detail: French 10-year government bond yields extended their rise to stand 16bp higher at 4.94%. The move follows weekend rioting across France and continuing political instability.

squawks.headline: Violent protests spread from France to Italy and Belgium, with looting and clashes in Milan, Brussels and Liège
squawks.detail: The FT reports looting and clashes with police in Milan, Brussels, Liège and Tirana as unrest spreads beyond France. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: China threatens to retaliate if the UK keeps restrictions on Chinese electric vehicles
squawks.detail: China's Commerce Ministry says it will firmly counter any UK move to press ahead with restrictive measures against Chinese EVs.

squawks.headline: US NAHB housing market index falls to 29 in October, below the 31 forecast and down from 32
squawks.detail: The US NAHB housing market index came in at 29, against a forecast of 31 and a previous reading of 32.

squawks.headline: Russia's Lavrov calls US and Israeli action against Iran baseless and offers help in resolving the crisis
squawks.detail: Russian foreign minister Lavrov said Moscow is ready to help find a way out of the crisis.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister accuses European countries of complicity in the US war with Iran
squawks.detail: Iran's foreign minister Araghchi also said Tehran would welcome any proposal that guarantees regional security without a foreign presence.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister says attacks on ships in the Caspian Sea are a serious concern and calls on Europe to drop double standards
squawks.detail: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi also said diplomacy is the only route open to the US in the dispute with Iran. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Russia's Lavrov calls for restoring free navigation through Hormuz and says neither Ukraine nor others are ready for talks
squawks.detail: Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov called for a return to pre-crisis conditions in the Middle East, including freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, and for Yemen negotiations to resume. He said Russia would prefer to reach its goals in Ukraine through talks, that it sticks to its investment and nuclear agreements with Iran, and that it has no interest in volatile energy prices.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister blames the US for Strait of Hormuz tensions and says Iran-US and Ukraine disputes need negotiated settlements
squawks.detail: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi said the US bears responsibility for insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz and that regional issues should be settled through diplomacy, according to state TV. He said Iran-US talks, Ukraine and the Hormuz situation came up in his discussions, and that both the Ukraine and Iran-US conflicts should be resolved by negotiation rather than war.

squawks.headline: Egypt's parliament delays its vote on military support for Saudi Arabia to 26 October
squawks.detail: Lawmakers said the Egyptian parliament has pushed back to 26 October its vote on letting the armed forces help defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks. The vote had been expected this week.

squawks.headline: Ukraine's foreign minister says Kyiv faces obstacles in getting interceptors against Russian ballistic missiles
squawks.detail: Ukraine's foreign minister said the country is running into obstacles in obtaining interceptors to counter Russian ballistic missiles.

squawks.headline: Chinese Premier urges all sides in the Iran conflict to choose peace and return to talks soon
squawks.detail: According to Xinhua, China's Premier said all parties concerned should opt for peace and resume dialogue and negotiations at an early date. He also said Beijing is ready to advance exchanges and cooperation with Iran.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says some types of essential US supplies to Ukraine are being delayed
squawks.detail: Ukraine's president said deliveries of some categories of essential supplies from the US have been delayed. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Egypt's parliament to vote this week on letting its armed forces help defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Egypt's parliament is expected to vote this week on authorising its military to help defend Saudi Arabia against attacks by Yemen's Houthis. The support would be given if Riyadh asks for it.

squawks.headline: White House adviser Hassett says US inflation appears to need more work again
squawks.detail: White House senior adviser Kevin Hassett said US inflation appears to need further work again. In the same remarks, he described discretionary travel as a sign that consumers feel confident.

squawks.headline: Swap pricing for a Bank of Canada rate hike in October falls to 68% from 74% after Canadian CPI data
squawks.detail: Swap market data put the chance of a Bank of Canada hike in October at 68%, down from 74% before the September inflation release.

squawks.headline: Canadian CPI rises 0.1% m/m in September, below the 0.2% forecast; CPI-trim slows to 1.8% and CPI-common to 2.4%
squawks.detail: Canada's September CPI rose 0.1% on the month against a 0.2% forecast, after -0.1% previously. CPI-trim came in at 1.8% (forecast 1.9%, previous 1.9%), CPI-common at 2.4% (previous 2.6%) and BoC core CPI at 2.2% y/y (previous 2.4%), with core flat on the month.

squawks.headline: Canadian CPI rises 3.1% y/y, below the 3.2% forecast; CPI-median measure at 1.9%
squawks.detail: Canada's annual CPI came in at 3.1%, against a 3.2% forecast and up from 3.0% previously. The CPI-median core measure was 1.9%, against a 2% forecast and down from 2.0%.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says UK household energy bills are due to rise again in January
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation says the next rise in household energy bills is due in January. It notes that 46% of domestic gas use falls in the first quarter of the year.

squawks.headline: Iraq's October oil exports average over 3.4m b/d so far, up from 3m b/d in September, reports say
squawks.detail: Reports put Iraq's crude exports at an average of more than 3.4 million barrels per day so far in October, compared with 3 million barrels per day in September.

squawks.headline: IRGC spokesman warns that even limited US action against Iran would set off a global energy crisis
squawks.detail: A spokesman for Iran's Revolutionary Guards gave the warning, Sepah News reported. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

squawks.headline: French PM says intelligence agencies warn the far left could try to disrupt the presidential election
squawks.detail: French PM Lecornu says intelligence agencies have briefed him on the risk. Separately, President Macron condemns looting and vandalism during cost-of-living protests and orders a review of intelligence and police preparedness.

squawks.headline: Iranian hardliners call for nuclear weapons after the killing of Supreme Leader Khamenei, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that hardliners in Iran are pushing to weaponise the enrichment programme. They say Khamenei, who had prohibited atomic bombs, has been killed.

squawks.headline: French PM Lecornu says the government would declare a state of emergency if it were judged necessary
squawks.detail: France's prime minister made the remark as rioting continues across the country. French bonds have already been under selling pressure today because of the unrest.

squawks.headline: Report says a breakthrough to halt US-Iran escalation is expected to be announced this week
squawks.detail: A market newswire reports that mediators are still working to narrow the points of contention between the US and Iran. The report names no source, and no market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: French PM Lecornu orders partial curfews after riots and says the finance ministry can fully fund short-time working
squawks.detail: French Prime Minister Lecornu said he had asked prefectures and some local authorities to impose partial curfews tonight, that the government will support business, and that the finance ministry can fund short-time working at 100%. He said about 80% of those still in custody will be prosecuted.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says a proposed Putin-Trump-Xi summit has no agenda or substantive agreements yet and a Ukraine deal needs Kyiv's participation
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said there is no agenda yet for the proposed summit of Putin, Trump and Xi, and no substantive agreements have been reached. It also said a final peace settlement for Ukraine is hardly possible unless someone from Kyiv's side takes part.

squawks.headline: French borrowing costs rise 0.1 percentage point as bond selling resumes; 10-year spread over Germany back at 1.45 percentage points
squawks.detail: The FT reports that French government bonds are under renewed selling pressure today, lifting borrowing costs by 0.1 percentage point. That takes the extra yield France pays over Germany on 10-year debt back up to 1.45 percentage points.

squawks.headline: Chancellor Healey reportedly weighs income tax on family business handovers before his first Budget
squawks.detail: City AM, citing a report, says Chancellor John Healey is considering charging income tax when owners pass companies to their children, which could nearly double the tax bill. The report says the plans are aimed at avoiding spending cuts.

squawks.headline: Ukraine's foreign minister says a Russia-China-US summit would only encourage Putin to keep fighting
squawks.detail: Ukraine's foreign minister criticised the proposed summit of Russia, China and the US, saying it would encourage Putin to continue the war. This follows reports that Putin has proposed a summit with Trump and Xi on Ukraine's future.

squawks.headline: PBOC governor says the bank will study moving its main open market operation tenor to overnight at an appropriate time
squawks.detail: China's central bank governor said the change would aim to make interest rate regulation more precise, according to Chinese state media.

squawks.headline: Trafigura economist puts Middle East crude flows 5m-7m b/d below pre-war levels and product flows 4m b/d lower
squawks.detail: The chief economist at commodity trader Trafigura gave the estimates for reduced Middle East crude and oil product flows compared with before the war.

squawks.headline: PBOC governor widens eligibility for standing lending facilities and plans to let overseas institutions trade RMB onshore
squawks.detail: The People's Bank of China governor also announced steps to promote bond market connectivity and to make it easier for overseas financial institutions to trade renminbi in China's domestic foreign exchange market, CCTV reported. The measures were announced alongside the liquidity support tool for non-bank institutions.

squawks.headline: PBOC governor says China will launch a liquidity support tool for large-scale redemptions at non-bank institutions
squawks.detail: The People's Bank of China governor announced plans for a liquidity facility to support non-bank financial institutions facing large-scale redemptions. No size or timing was given.

squawks.headline: Goldman Sachs says its cross-asset sentiment and positioning gauge falls to its lowest since April
squawks.detail: Goldman Sachs says its sentiment and positioning indicator has fallen to its lowest level since April and has decoupled from strong global PMIs. The bank points to stronger fixed income fund flows, positioning in gold and the yen, and a sharp fall in hedge fund net leverage.

squawks.headline: US Secretary of State Rubio says Ukraine and Russia should concentrate on ending the war
squawks.detail: Rubio made the remarks on arriving in Uzbekistan for meetings with officials of the C5+1 grouping of the US and post-Soviet Central Asian states, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: UBS now expects the ECB to raise rates by 25bp in March 2027 after a December hike
squawks.detail: UBS has changed its ECB call. It previously expected the hiking cycle to end in December and now also expects a 25bp increase in March 2027.

squawks.headline: Brent drops below $105 a barrel, down 2.43% on the day; WTI falls 2.21% to $96.76
squawks.detail: Brent crude fell under $105.00 a barrel in early European trading, a 2.43% fall on the day. WTI fell 2.21% to $96.76 a barrel.

squawks.headline: CFTC data show speculators' largest net euro short since January 2016, SocGen says, with the market heavily long dollars
squawks.detail: SocGen says the latest CFTC positioning data show the biggest net short position in the euro since January 2016. It adds that the market is also holding large long positions in the dollar.

squawks.headline: China says it will hold talks to set up a dialogue mechanism on export controls
squawks.detail: Market headlines on 19 October report that China plans talks on an export-control dialogue mechanism. The reports do not say who the other party is. This follows its earlier announcement of changes to export controls on dual-use items, effective 18 November.

squawks.headline: Russia strikes energy facilities in 11 Ukrainian regions overnight, Ukraine's deputy energy minister says
squawks.detail: Ukraine's deputy energy minister reported overnight Russian attacks on energy infrastructure across 11 regions. Russia's chief of general staff had earlier told Putin that strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities had begun.

squawks.headline: China expected to hold benchmark lending rates for a 17th straight month in October, Reuters poll shows
squawks.detail: A Reuters survey shows China is expected to keep its benchmark lending rates unchanged in October. Reuters says Q3 GDP came in stronger than expected, which reduced the chances of easing in the near term.

squawks.headline: Average UK two-year fixed mortgage rate climbs to 5.55% from 5.29% a month ago, homes portal data show
squawks.detail: Data from a homes portal reported by City AM put the average two-year fixed rate at 5.55%, compared with 5.29% last month and 4.25% before the war in Iran. The report says sellers are cutting asking prices as higher rates weigh on the housing market.

squawks.headline: China's Commerce Ministry announces changes to export control work on dual-use items, effective 18 November
squawks.detail: China's Commerce Ministry has announced further changes to how it identifies and handles export control concerns for dual-use items. It says the announcement takes effect officially on 18 November.

squawks.headline: Euro stays under selling pressure against sterling as French political instability continues
squawks.detail: A market commentary headline reports continued selling of the euro against sterling, linked to political instability in France after weekend rioting. No levels were given.

squawks.headline: US Secretary of State Rubio says Trump will consider any route to ending the Ukraine war and intelligence sharing with Kyiv continues
squawks.detail: Rubio said the US would keep looking for chances to end the conflict but did not confirm details of a proposed meeting. He also said intelligence sharing with Ukraine has not been paused.

squawks.headline: BoE examines Barclays after complaint that traders understated the risk of private credit exposure, FT reports
squawks.detail: The FT reports that the Bank of England received a complaint that Barclays understated the risk of derivatives it used to finance private credit loans, and is scrutinising the lender's disclosures.

squawks.headline: China Q3 GDP grows 4.5% y/y, beating the 4.4% poll; September retail sales rise 1.1% y/y and industrial output 5.5%
squawks.detail: China's statistics bureau reports Q3 GDP up 4.5% y/y, compared with 4.3% previously, and up 1.2% q/q. In September the jobless rate eased to 5.2% from 5.3%, while fixed-asset investment for January to September fell 7.2% y/y and property investment fell 20.6%.

squawks.headline: China's new home prices fall 2.8% y/y in September, a smaller drop than August's 3.0%
squawks.detail: A source calculation based on statistics bureau data shows the 2.8% annual fall. In Shenzhen prices fell 1.0% y/y but rose 0.3% m/m, and in Guangzhou they fell 1.1% y/y and rose 0.2% m/m.

squawks.headline: Brent slips 1.7% to $108 a barrel and WTI falls to near $97.50 in Asian trading
squawks.detail: Market reports said traders were weighing Middle East tensions against fairly stable regional supplies, and one report linked the WTI fall to the US waiver on Russian oil sanctions. US 10-year Treasury yields held at 5.06% as expectations of an imminent Fed rate rise eased.

squawks.headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says sanctions on Russian crude stay in place and the exemptions cover diesel only
squawks.detail: Wright said the recent exemptions apply only to diesel supplies under General Licence 135, issued on 9 October, which permits certain transactions in Russian-origin diesel to ease global shortages.

squawks.headline: Japan's PM Takaichi says JGB issuance will be kept at an appropriate level and she has no fixed view on an extra budget
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Takaichi said she has no preconceived position on whether the government will compile a supplementary budget. She added that building a robust economy can strengthen market confidence in the yen.

squawks.headline: French 10-year bond futures fall and the euro eases after weekend rioting across France
squawks.detail: French 10-year note futures dropped in early Asian trading after unrest in France over the weekend, according to market reports. Reuters reported that the euro eased in the wake of the rioting.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says the bond taper approach is unchanged and declines to preannounce timing of any emergency JGB market measures
squawks.detail: The BoJ Governor said the bank will look at market conditions, including how fast long-term rates rise and signs of instability, when deciding whether to intervene. He added that long-term rates would probably rise steadily if the bank raises its short-term rate, and that setting policy properly to reach the 2% target would help stabilise the JGB market.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says underlying inflation is near 2% and the Middle East conflict is adding to energy-led price pressures
squawks.detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said Japan is seeing a positive cycle of rising wages and recovering prices, and that anchoring underlying inflation around 2% is becoming more important. He said strong global demand and a tight labour market are also adding to inflation; dollar/yen was reported 0.19% lower at 157.72.

squawks.headline: Putin proposes a summit with Trump and Xi on Ukraine's future, WSJ reports
squawks.detail: The Wall Street Journal reported that Russian President Putin has asked Trump and Chinese President Xi for a three-way meeting to decide Ukraine's future.

squawks.headline: RBA's Kent says neutral rates appear to be rising in Australia and abroad and questions whether policy is restrictive enough
squawks.detail: Reserve Bank of Australia Assistant Governor Kent said policy is somewhat restrictive but it is unclear whether it is restrictive enough, and the RBA faces a hard trade-off between inflation and unemployment. He said household demand is softening while business credit stays strong, and that long-term inflation expectations look well anchored.

squawks.headline: UK-listed company profit warnings hit their highest level in nearly two years as energy costs rise, EY says
squawks.detail: EY analysis shows London-listed companies issued 65 profit warnings over the summer, up from 59 in the second quarter, with higher energy costs linked to the Iran war among the causes cited.

squawks.headline: Trump says his recent Russia moves are meant to keep Moscow in peace talks and reports great progress
squawks.detail: Trump said signing a Russia document now could push Moscow out of the talks, told Russia to stay away from supporting Iran, and criticised Ukraine's strikes on Russian diesel refineries for hurting global diesel markets. Separately, the UK reaffirmed its support for tougher sanctions on Russia.

squawks.headline: Zelenskyy offers to stop strikes on Russian refineries if the US sends more interceptors and accuses Trump of pushing Ukraine to capitulate
squawks.detail: Ukraine's president proposed halting strikes on Russian oil refineries in return for more air-defence interceptors. He cited delayed Patriot deliveries, Starlink restrictions and eased Russia-related sanctions as US pressure for concessions to Russia.

squawks.headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says enforcement of the Graham sanctions on Russia is suspended for now, not ended
squawks.detail: Wright said extra Russian diesel exports would benefit US consumers and the world. He described the US-Russia diesel deal, agreed before Russia moved to scale back the war, as an innovative route to peace.

squawks.headline: City of London Corporation considers tax rises and service cuts to close a £70mn budget gap
squawks.detail: The FT reports that the Corporation is preparing for the government's overhaul of local authority funding, and that the Barbican Centre's future is uncertain.

squawks.headline: UK Foreign Office now advises against all but essential travel to Saudi Arabia
squawks.detail: The UK Foreign Office has changed its travel advice for Saudi Arabia to advise against all but essential travel. The change follows reports earlier in the day of missiles and drones aimed at Riyadh and the Yanbu export hub.

squawks.headline: Trump says the Iran conflict will be over very soon
squawks.detail: US President Trump said the situation with Iran will end very soon. He gave no timetable or details.

squawks.headline: US TIC data show China's Treasury holdings fall to $591bn and Japan's to $1.068trn in August; UK holdings rise to $1.010trn
squawks.detail: US Treasury TIC data show China's holdings of US Treasuries at $591bn in August against $618bn in July, Japan's at $1.068trn against $1.104trn, and the UK's at $1.010trn against $998bn. Net foreign holdings of Treasury bonds and notes rose by $108.9bn in August after falling by $3.6bn in July.

squawks.headline: US TIC data show net long-term inflows of $279.2bn, up from -$27.9bn; overall net capital flows at $199.8bn
squawks.detail: US Treasury International Capital data put net long-term transactions at $279.2bn, against -$27.9bn previously. Overall net capital flows came in at $199.8bn, compared with a revised $87.4bn the previous month.

squawks.headline: Brent crude futures settle up $3.94, or 3.72%, at $109.86 a barrel
squawks.detail: Brent crude futures settle at $109.86 a barrel, up $3.94 or 3.72% on the session.

squawks.headline: US net interest payments on debt reach a record $1.05trn in fiscal 2026
squawks.detail: The US paid a record $1.05trn in net interest on its debt in the 2026 fiscal year, according to the US budget figures.

squawks.headline: Brent futures reach $110 a barrel for the first time since 20 May
squawks.detail: Brent futures rose to $110 a barrel, a level last seen on 20 May, extending the day's gains.

squawks.headline: WTI crude futures settle up $3.44, or 3.51%, at $101.41 a barrel
squawks.detail: NYMEX WTI crude futures settled at $101.41 a barrel, up $3.44 or 3.51%. November diesel futures settled at $4.8991 a gallon and November gasoline at $3.2354 a gallon.

squawks.headline: US CENTCOM commander says the US naval blockade has halted all of Iran's maritime exports and imports
squawks.detail: The commander of US Central Command said in a post on X that Iran currently has no seaborne exports or imports because of the US naval blockade. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US CENTCOM says over 100m barrels of oil were shipped through Hormuz in the past 7 days with US help
squawks.detail: US Central Command said the US has helped move more than 100m barrels through the Strait of Hormuz over the past seven days. US officials also said about 400 merchant ships transited the strait in that period.

squawks.headline: US posts a $26.9bn budget deficit for September
squawks.detail: The US Treasury reported a September budget deficit of $26.9bn, the final month of a fiscal year in which the deficit reached $1.992trn.

squawks.headline: EU's von der Leyen says the Commission will propose import curbs on further Chinese sectors
squawks.detail: European Commission President von der Leyen said on Friday that the Commission will propose curbs on Chinese imports that go beyond the safeguard measures agreed with Beijing to halve shipments of Chinese hybrid cars.

squawks.headline: US fiscal 2026 deficit widens to $1.992trn from $1.775trn; gross interest on debt hits a record $1.36trn
squawks.detail: The US Treasury puts the fiscal 2026 deficit at $1.992trn, against $1.775trn in fiscal 2025, with net customs receipts of $173.22bn compared with $194.87bn. Gross interest on the debt reached a record $1.36trn, up $144bn or 12% on the previous year.

squawks.headline: Iran says it is ready to help resolve the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen
squawks.detail: A market news account reported that Iran has offered to help settle the Saudi-Yemen conflict. The post did not say which Iranian official made the offer. The offer follows the Saudi-led coalition's report that it intercepted missiles and drones aimed at Riyadh and the Yanbu export hub.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says the UK has had the equivalent of 13 years of normal inflation in five years
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation says the UK has had about 13 years' worth of normal inflation over the past five years. It also says the cost of living crisis hit the UK harder than other countries.

squawks.headline: European Council President Costa calls for the EU long-term budget to be agreed by year-end
squawks.detail: European Council President Costa said the EU's long-term budget needs to be agreed by the end of the year.

squawks.headline: EU's von der Leyen puts Ukraine's funding gap for 2027 at 70bn
squawks.detail: European Commission President von der Leyen gave the 70bn figure for Ukraine's 2027 funding shortfall. EU leaders have asked the Commission for a proposal on Ukraine's additional financing needs for that year.

squawks.headline: Trump says Russia will release diesel under the US-Russia deal and calls it a deal for the world
squawks.detail: The US President was speaking to reporters on Friday about the US-Russia diesel deal. Other leaders had criticised the deal earlier in the day.

squawks.headline: IMF head calls for global cooperation on risks from AI and the prolonged Middle East war
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that the IMF Managing Director on Friday urged global leaders to cooperate in the face of several economic risks, including rapid advances in AI and a prolonged war in the Middle East. Washington pointed to what it calls US-led economic momentum.

squawks.headline: France's Macron says an EU budget deal is possible by year-end and argues against a March summit before the French election
squawks.detail: The French President said agreement on the EU budget could be reached by the end of the year. He said holding the budget deal summit in March, weeks before the French election, would not be a good approach.

squawks.headline: EU's von der Leyen says the bloc will work on new instruments to tackle the trade imbalance with China
squawks.detail: The European Commission President said on Friday that the EU would develop new instruments to address its trade imbalance with China. She spoke after an EU leaders' meeting.

squawks.headline: France's Macron says the US-Russia diesel deal is unhelpful and breeds doubt and defiance
squawks.detail: French President Macron criticised the US diesel deal with Russia on Friday. Ukraine's Zelensky and US lawmakers had already objected to the deal.

squawks.headline: EU's von der Leyen calls the China trade imbalance structural and unsustainable and says EU leaders are united on China
squawks.detail: European Commission President von der Leyen spoke after China's commerce ministry warned the EU against applying pressure.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US was not behind limits on Ukraine's access to the Starshield system
squawks.detail: US President Trump said the US did not restrict Ukraine's access to the Starshield system and that he does not know who ordered it.

squawks.headline: EU leaders ask the Commission for a proposal on Ukraine's extra 2027 financing needs; Costa says Russia's actions point to escalation
squawks.detail: European Council President Costa said EU leaders have asked the European Commission to put forward a proposal covering Ukraine's additional financing needs for 2027. He also said Russia's actions indicate escalation.

squawks.headline: Trump says oil prices will come down very soon
squawks.detail: US President Trump said oil prices would fall soon. He made the remarks while discussing inflation, as US crude traded at a session high.

squawks.headline: US crude futures jump more than $3 to a session high of $101.02, the highest since 21 September
squawks.detail: US crude futures rose by more than $3 to $101.02 a barrel in late trading on Friday, according to a market wire report. This is their highest level since 21 September.

squawks.headline: FT says the financial sector's lobbying against a possible UK bank tax rise in the Budget may have been hurt by splits among big lenders
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that bankers are uneasy about a possible tax rise in the forthcoming Budget. It says the sector's lobbying may have been weakened by divisions between the large lenders.

squawks.headline: Brent jumps more than $3 to a new session high of $109.58 a barrel
squawks.detail: Brent crude futures rose more than $3 to a session high of $109.58 a barrel. US crude futures gained more than $2 to go above $100, with reports citing ongoing Middle East supply concerns and an outage at a Russian refinery.

squawks.headline: Oil extends gains as US crude climbs above $100 a barrel
squawks.detail: Oil prices extended their gains in late trading on 16 October, and US crude rose above $100 a barrel.

squawks.headline: Putin orders the military to keep up massive strikes on Ukraine's defence industry and logistics centres
squawks.detail: Russian President Vladimir Putin told the military to keep carrying out massive and group strikes on Ukraine's military-industrial sites and logistics centres, according to reports. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Scottish government is set to drop its opposition to new North Sea oil and gas fields, Politico reports
squawks.detail: Politico reports that the Scottish government is preparing to drop its opposition to developing new oil and gas fields. No timing or further detail was given.

squawks.headline: Putin says Russia's offensive is running along the whole front line at a faster pace and calls the capture of Dobropillya significant
squawks.detail: Russian reports say Putin described taking Dobropillya as opening the way to the DPR's borders, said taking the DPR remains a main task and called for better protection of civilian infrastructure. Russia's chief of general staff Gerasimov said the armed forces had launched massive strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities.

squawks.headline: Brent climbs to session highs and trades near $107 a barrel
squawks.detail: Market reports say oil prices rose to their highs of the session, with Brent near $107/bbl. The move came as Russian officials reported strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

squawks.headline: Russia's Gerasimov tells Putin the army has begun strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities and plans to hit strategic bridges
squawks.detail: Russia's Chief of the General Staff, Valery Gerasimov, reported to President Putin that strikes on Ukraine's energy facilities have begun and that strategic bridges are also planned targets, according to reports from Russia.

squawks.headline: France-Germany car deal seeks to dilute EU 2035 CO2 targets and opens the way for UK trusted-partner status under Made in EU rules
squawks.detail: France and Germany said on Friday that their car industry agreement would water down EU-wide CO2 emission targets for 2035. It would also open the door for Britain to be treated as a trusted partner under the EU's Made in EU rules, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: US lawmakers introduce a bill to block Trump's diesel deal with Russia
squawks.detail: A bill to block the Trump administration's diesel deal with Russia has been introduced in Congress. Its sponsors are mostly Democrats, with one Republican among them.

squawks.headline: Putin says Russian forces fully control Luhansk; Kremlin says 450 km of a 660 km border security strip is under Russian control
squawks.detail: Putin said the Luhansk region is now entirely under the control of Russian forces and that work on the security zone along the Ukrainian border is going well. The Kremlin said the strip runs for 660 km, of which 450 km is currently held by Russia.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says Russia's security zone will not be part of any Ukraine negotiation; Putin says 10% of Donetsk is still to be taken
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said the security zone Russia is building will not be up for negotiation with Ukraine. It also quoted Putin as saying Russian forces have yet to take 10% of the Donetsk region, and Putin said 310 populated areas have been captured since the start of the year.

squawks.headline: Italy and the European Commission agree on a gas price cap law
squawks.detail: Italy and the European Commission have reached agreement on a law capping gas prices, according to a market news feed. The report gave no details of the terms.

squawks.headline: UK consumer confidence slips to a five-month low in October, LSEG/Ipsos survey shows
squawks.detail: The monthly LSEG/Ipsos survey shows UK consumer confidence edged lower in October to its weakest level in five months. The post gave no index figure.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz says Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy and communications targets are understandable; EU weighs Russian visa curbs
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Merz said Ukraine attacking Russian targets that hinder its war effort, including energy and communications infrastructure, is understandable. He said the EU summit is discussing restrictions on issuing visas to Russians and that there is still room for manoeuvre.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz says a 90bn loan will not cover Ukraine's needs and the Commission will assess its financial aid needs
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Merz said the European Commission will assess over the coming weeks how much financial aid Ukraine needs. He said a 90bn loan would not be enough.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz says Italy largely backs the German-French plan to phase out coal-fired power stations by 2035
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Merz said Italy is largely in agreement with a joint German-French proposal to phase out coal-fired power generation by 2035.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz says the EU budget needs further cuts and expects another European Council meeting in November
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Merz said the European budget must be reduced further and that additional European Council meetings are expected in November. He said he hopes for a budget agreement before the end of the year but is not sure it will happen.

squawks.headline: Putin envoy Dmitriev says Russia and the US are discussing joint data centre projects and will announce more initiatives soon
squawks.detail: Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev said the projects could draw on power from Russian nuclear stations. He said further joint initiatives beyond the diesel deal would be announced soon, and some would go ahead before Russia's military operation in Ukraine ends.

squawks.headline: NatWest is no longer a US Treasury primary dealer, New York Fed says
squawks.detail: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York's list shows NatWest has stopped being a primary dealer.

squawks.headline: US Energy Department seeks an exchange of up to 17m barrels of crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve
squawks.detail: The US Department of Energy is offering up to 17m barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve through an exchange, according to wire headlines.

squawks.headline: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted missiles and drones aimed at Riyadh, the Yanbu export hub and southern Saudi Arabia
squawks.detail: The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed two cruise missiles over the Red Sea, a ballistic missile launched towards Yanbu, and three drones over the southern and Riyadh regions. Saudi Arabia said Riyadh, Yanbu and southern areas had been targeted; no market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Putin envoy Dmitriev says the Graham sanctions bill blocks Russia-US investment cooperation
squawks.detail: Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev said the sanctions bill sponsored by the late Senator Graham blocks Russia-US investment cooperation. He said there was growing recognition in the US that the bill was a mistake.

squawks.headline: German foreign minister says Europe is in Iran's sights and Iran's hostile activities will not be tolerated
squawks.detail: Germany's foreign minister made the remarks on Friday in the same appearance as his comments on Ukraine, the EU budget talks and the Mercosur deal. He also said it is imperative that EU budget negotiations are concluded this year.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says the neutral rate estimate will reflect how past hikes have fed through to financial conditions and prices
squawks.detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said he wants to assess the neutral rate estimate in light of the cumulative effect of earlier rate rises on financial conditions and domestic prices. He also said underlying inflation being quite close to 2% marks the policy shift.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says G20 talks did not depart from the bank's baseline and FX, AI and the Middle East will set the timing of hikes
squawks.detail: BoJ Governor Ueda said nothing he heard at this week's meetings deviated from the bank's baseline view, and he saw no big gap with global policymakers on inflationary pressure from AI demand. He said the timing and pace of further rate rises will depend on the effects of currency moves, AI demand and Middle East developments on prices.

squawks.headline: Zelensky says Putin has no interest in ending the war and Donbas would not be enough for Russia; open to talks in Budapest
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelensky said Putin is playing with words and does not want the war to end, and the issue goes beyond withdrawal from Donbas. He said he would not mind going to Budapest, wants several negotiation tracks, and said European allies have enough Patriot interceptors for Ukraine to get through winter.

squawks.headline: Putin envoy Dmitriev says Zelensky has overplayed his hand and is an obstacle to peace as peacemaking speeds up
squawks.detail: Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev said Zelensky's attacks on President Trump would have significant consequences, and described peacemaking efforts as accelerating. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Hungary's PM Magyar says Budapest is ready to help diplomatically towards a Ukraine ceasefire and will continue talks with Kyiv
squawks.detail: Hungarian Prime Minister Magyar said he agreed with Zelensky to continue talks at ministerial level and to put relations on a new footing, and he expressed solidarity with Ukraine over Russia's aggression. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Reports say John Healey is drawing up plans to tax banks in the forthcoming Budget
squawks.detail: City AM reports that John Healey is weighing options to raise more tax from the banking industry in the forthcoming Budget. City AM says senior banking figures have warned against the plans.

squawks.headline: Kremlin's Peskov says Zelensky is not seeking a peaceful settlement and Russia shares Trump's view on this
squawks.detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said the Ukrainian president does not want to take responsibility or pursue a peaceful resolution, and that Moscow agrees with Trump on the point.

squawks.headline: US Treasury funds take in $3.6bn in the week, their 16th straight weekly inflow, BofA says
squawks.detail: BofA, citing EPFR data, said total bond fund inflows came to $11.8bn in the week to Wednesday. Equity funds took in $64.5bn over the same period.

squawks.headline: Eurozone final CPI is confirmed at 0.6% m/m in September, in line with forecast and up from 0.4%
squawks.detail: The final September eurozone figure showed consumer prices up 0.6% on the month, matching the 0.4% previous reading's forecast path at 0.6%. The annual rate was confirmed at 3.8%.

squawks.headline: Putin envoy Dmitriev says the US Treasury asked Russia's RDIF fund to help facilitate the US-Russia diesel deal
squawks.detail: Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev said the US finance ministry asked the Russian Direct Investment Fund, which he heads, to facilitate the diesel deal between the two countries. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Putin envoy Dmitriev says Russia and the US are discussing Arctic and LNG projects
squawks.detail: Kirill Dmitriev, the Kremlin's envoy, said Russia and the US are in talks on projects in the Arctic and on liquefied natural gas. The remarks follow the recently reported US-Russia diesel deal.

squawks.headline: Russia's Novak says Russian diesel will help balance the global market and the deal with the US benefits all fuel consumers
squawks.detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak made the remarks about the US-Russia diesel deal on 16 October.

squawks.headline: US industrial production rises 2.25% y/y in September, up from 1.42% the previous month
squawks.detail: The annual figure for US industrial production in September was 2.25%, up from 1.42% in the previous reading. No forecast was given.

squawks.headline: US Treasury yields rise after economic data, with the 10-year up 3.8bp to 5.125%
squawks.detail: The US 10-year yield rose 3.8bp to 5.125% after economic data. The 30-year rose 3.04bp to 5.458%, the 2-year rose 1.45bp to 4.766%, and the 2s10s spread stood at +35.7bp.

squawks.headline: US industrial production rises 0.7% m/m in September, above the 0.4% forecast; capacity utilisation at 76.9%
squawks.detail: US industrial production rose 0.7% m/m in September, after 0.0% the previous month and above the 0.4% forecast. Manufacturing output rose 0.3%, in line with forecast, after -0.3%. Capacity utilisation came in at 76.9%, against a 76.5% forecast and 76.3% previously.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says lower net migration will hit fiscal headroom ahead of the Budget
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation says lower net migration will cut fiscal headroom in the upcoming Budget. This adds to its earlier estimate that headroom has halved to about £12bn in 2029-30 before Budget measures.

squawks.headline: SNB's Tschudin says Swiss inflation pressure is slightly higher than in June
squawks.detail: Petra Tschudin of the Swiss National Bank's governing board said inflationary pressure in Switzerland is a little higher than it was in June.

squawks.headline: Bank of Italy raises Italy's 2026 GDP growth forecast to 1% from 0.6% and its 2027 forecast to 0.7% from 0.4%
squawks.detail: The Bank of Italy has raised its 2026 growth forecast for Italy to 1%, up from the 0.6% it projected in June. It has also lifted its 2027 forecast to 0.7% from 0.4%.

squawks.headline: German foreign minister says the US is still supporting Ukraine and Kyiv and Moscow will in the end have to negotiate
squawks.detail: Germany's foreign minister was asked about relations between Trump and Ukraine. He said the US is essentially still providing support to Ukraine and that Ukraine and Russia will ultimately have to negotiate.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US may need to strike Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site but rules out nuclear weapons and ground troops
squawks.detail: In a Newsmax interview reported by Reuters, President Trump said the US may target the fortified underground site near one of Tehran's main nuclear facilities. He said the US would not use a nuclear bomb and was not considering sending ground troops to Iran.

squawks.headline: German foreign minister says accommodating Putin would be the wrong signal and warns Russia's Black Sea actions put food supplies at risk
squawks.detail: Germany's foreign minister also says the Mercosur trade deal is already delivering positive results and that EU budget negotiations must be concluded this year.

squawks.headline: US natural gas futures drop 5% after a force majeure is lifted
squawks.detail: A market wire reports that US natural gas futures fell 5% after a force majeure was lifted. The report does not say which facility was affected.

squawks.headline: US import prices rise 1.1% m/m in September and export prices jump 2.2%, both above forecast
squawks.detail: US import prices rose 1.1% m/m against a 1% forecast and 0.7% previously. Export prices rose 2.2% m/m against a 0.9% forecast and 0.6% previously.

squawks.headline: Kalshi odds of an October Fed hike fall to 13% from 55% after Fed Chair Warsh's remarks
squawks.detail: Prediction market Kalshi puts the probability of a Fed hold in October at 86%, up from 50%, following Fed Chair Warsh's comments, according to a market commentary account.

squawks.headline: Canadian housing starts rise to an annualised 248.896K in September, above the 232.5K forecast
squawks.detail: Canada's September housing starts came in at an annualised 248.896K, compared with a forecast of 232.5K and 229.0K the month before.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says there is no evidence the neutral rate sits at any specific level
squawks.detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said there is no evidence that the neutral rate is around any particular level. He also said a policy shift comes when underlying inflation is close to 2%.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says underlying inflation cannot be allowed to rise further above 2% and the focus is now on entrenching 2%
squawks.detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda also said he wants to judge the estimate of the neutral rate after taking account of the cumulative effect of past rate rises on financial conditions and domestic prices.

squawks.headline: China's commerce ministry warns the EU it will not gain from pressure and should not underestimate China's resolve
squawks.detail: China's commerce ministry said the EU should not expect to win concessions by pressuring China, and that Beijing is determined and able to protect its interests.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says the next meeting will consider changing the view that underlying inflation is nearing 2%
squawks.detail: BoJ Governor Ueda said the bank heard nothing at this week's meetings that departed from its baseline view, and that the timing and pace of further hikes will depend on how FX, AI demand and Middle East developments affect prices. He also said financial conditions remain accommodative.

squawks.headline: Zelensky calls the US-Russia diesel deal inappropriate, expects a gas deal to follow and rejects any deal on frozen Russian assets
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelensky said Ukraine cannot risk any deals on frozen Russian assets. He also said taking Donbas would not satisfy Putin and called current efforts to end the war a parody.
